entry.title: Combined summary - BIP Proposal: Stateless PSBT Coordination (Blind Relay)
entry.summary: Coordinating multisignature Bitcoin transactions across various hardware and software wallets presents significant operational challenges, often requiring manual transfer of files or dependence on centralized servers. A new approach is being proposed through the Stateless PSBT Coordination draft BIP, which introduces a "Blind Relay" model utilizing an ephemeral, end-to-end encrypted WebSocket architecture. This model ensures that the relay server remains entirely unaware of any sensitive data, such as Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs), extended public keys (xpubs), or cryptographic signatures. By adopting a zero-knowledge operation, all transaction-related information is deleted immediately upon room closure or after 24 hours, mitigating risks associated with data persistence and privacy breaches. Furthermore, the protocol enhances operational security by requiring users to share the room URL and decryption key independently, outside the platform’s scope. Community engagement is sought for feedback on the draft BIP, available at [bip-stateless-psbt-coordination](https://github.com/scarlin90/bip-stateless-psbt-coordination). Contributions are encouraged regarding user experience, operational security tradeoffs, and suggestions for additional features or refinements to the reference implementation, aiming to improve the standard’s robustness and usability. The release of Signing Room version 2.0.0 brings considerable advancements, particularly in accessibility and integration simplicity. Among the notable features is a drop-in web component, allowing developers to integrate Signing Room functionality into their platforms using a single HTML tag. This enhancement streamlines deployment and broadens the potential user base. Detailed information about these improvements can be found in the [release notes](https://github.com/scarlin90/signingroom/releases/tag/v2.0.0), which provide comprehensive documentation for users and developers alike. Version 1.0.0 of the `@signing-room/sdk` represents a substantial leap forward in enabling cryptographic operations and coordination logic for signing ceremonies, decoupled from the main Angular client. The TypeScript SDK is framework-agnostic, permitting programmatic orchestration of ephemeral, end-to-end encrypted PSBT coordination ceremonies. Integration with the standard web UI allows real-time synchronization of actions such as room creation, participant joining, and signature uploads. The SDK supports advanced use cases, including headless multisig automation where AI agents can perform signing steps under human supervision. Developers benefit from extensive resources: the SDK repository is on [GitHub](https://github.com/scarlin90/signingroom/tree/main/libs/sdk), the package is available via [NPM](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@signing-room/sdk?activeTab=readme), and a detailed [YouTube walkthrough](https://youtu.be/yzcFlK6c6t0) demonstrates setup and usage. The walkthrough explains the architectural design, dynamic room management, and generating SHA-256 cryptographic integrity seals that anchor event logs to finalized transaction hexes, enhancing auditability and security. Developer feedback on API design and feature requests remains actively welcomed. Recent updates have further strengthened security and access control within the Signing Room ecosystem and the stateless PSBT coordination protocol. Version 3.4.0 of the coordinator and 1.2.0 of the SDK introduce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), eliminating reliance on persistent accounts or database states and guarding participant identities during the relay process. The access model has evolved beyond simple Coordinator and Guest roles to allow nuanced permissions suitable for high-security environments, such as institutional or legal multisig arrangements. These enhancements permit inclusion of off-chain witnesses or compliance officers who can verify signatures and outputs without having the capability to alter transaction state. RBAC is enforced through role-scoped capability tokens generated by the room initiator, derived from session entropy, and embedded within browser URL fragments—never transmitted over HTTP. Tokens define granular policy scopes like `can_propose`, `can_sign`, or `witness_only`, and enforcement is managed ephemerally in relay RAM. Unauthorized attempts to submit signatures are promptly rejected. Technical specifications and implementation guidance are provided in the [v3.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/scarlin90/signingroom/releases/tag/v3.4.0), and the updated BIP draft details the revised token schema and message formats, available at [BIP Draft Update](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://github.com/scarlin90/bip-stateless-psbt-coordination/blob/main/bip-draft.md&utm_source=gemini). Ongoing work is focused on Tapscript and BIP 371 support, expanding utility beyond native SegWit multisig and preparing for future enhancements like Miniscript spending trees. Input on token derivation methods and message formatting is encouraged to shape the next phases of development. The most recent milestone, marked by the release of Signing Room coordinator v4.2.0 and SDK v2.2.0, delivers end-to-end support for two-round MuSig2 Tap
